title: Multiple Findings in One Scene
summary: Teach the reviewer that a single scene may legitimately contain multiple independent findings and each must be evaluated separately.
learningObjectives: Recognize multiple findings in a single scene.
Avoid stopping after the first detected issue.

definitions.finding: An independently reportable observation supported by evidence.
definitions.compoundScene: A scene containing multiple reviewable events.
definitions.duplicateFinding: The same finding reported more than once.
definitions.independentFinding: A unique finding supported by separate evidence.

reviewerPrinciples: A scene may contain zero, one, or many findings.
Each finding requires its own evidence.
reviewerQuestions: Have all independent findings been identified?
Does each finding have separate evidence?
Can each finding stand alone in the report?
Would another reviewer identify the same number of findings?

decisionTree.question: Can each event be independently supported?

examples.text: A child is threatened with a weapon while drugs are being sold.
One insult repeated several times in the same exchange.

counterExamples.text: Report one finding because the first violation was detected.
Create five identical findings for one repeated insult.

questions.question: Can one scene contain multiple valid findings?
Should duplicate findings be reported separately?
Must each finding have its own evidence?
